name: PharmCAT (Pharmacogenomics Clinical Annotation Tool)

version.value: PharmCAT v3.4.0 (as named on the documentation home page)

scope: A software tool: it reads a VCF from sequencing or genotyping, identifies pharmacogenomic genotypes and infers haplotypes (star alleles), then uses the diplotypes to predict phenotypes and reports drug-prescribing recommendations from CPIC guidelines and from ClinPGx-annotated DPWG and FDA sources. Its documentation covers VCF requirements, calling of CYP2D6 and HLA by outside callers, and allele-frequency analysis.
mapping_methods: Matches VCF genotypes at allele-defining positions to named allele definitions and translates diplotypes to phenotype categories using the guideline tables.

licence.name: Not retrieved: the documentation pages were read but the software licence file was not.

update_frequency: Versioned releases (a changelog and versioning page are linked from the documentation).
coverage_limitations: Limited to the genes and drugs for which CPIC, DPWG or FDA recommendations exist
CYP2D6 and HLA calls come from outside callers; structural alleles are not called from a short-read VCF alone
known_omissions: The software and its bundled definitions are not installed; the same allele definitions are held through the CPIC API tables and PharmVar

reuse_decision.rationale: A tool that applies the allele definitions and guidelines already held through CPIC, PharmVar and ClinPGx; it carries no evidence that is not in those sources. It is the reference implementation to run, or to compare a future allele caller with, when a pharmacogenomic analysis is built.

mechanism_evidence.note: applies curated allele definitions and guideline tables; a method, not a new assertion

evidence_profile.biological_context: A method that applies published allele definitions and guidelines to a genotype; the clinical meaning is that of the guidelines, specific to the gene and the drug.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Inherited from the guidelines it applies; a calling pipeline adds the risk of wrong calls at positions it cannot see.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: As for the CPIC and PharmVar tables it uses: moderate at the haplotype level, low for variants outside the definitions.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: Predicted metaboliser or risk phenotype and a recommendation for a diplotype, drug-specific.
evidence_profile.absence_means: A gene, drug or allele outside the covered set receives no report; an uncalled position is treated according to the tool's rules, which can default to the reference allele.

overlaps_with_sources.note: applies the CPIC allele definitions and guideline tables; the evidence is the CPIC evidence, so count it once
